title: 128 Evaluation of lifetime feed efficiency and feeding behavior in Katahdin sheep
content:
Abstract
Feed efficiency remains one of the most economically important traits in commercial livestock production systems, as feed contributes up to 80-85% of livestock production costs. Potential exists to improve lifetime ewe production and minimize input costs by utilizing genetic selection focused on feed efficiency. The Vytelle Sense system allows measurement of individual animal DMI and feeding behavior variables. The aim of this study was to identify if measuring an individual’s postweaning residual feed intake (RFI) would subsequently predict RFI, gain:feed (G:F), and daily DMI as a lactating ewe. Katahdin ewes (Mature LowRFI: n = 7; Mature HighRFI: n = 6; Yearling LowRFI: n = 7; Yearling HighRFI: n = 4) previously evaluated on a Vytelle Sense system as lambs were mated to Katahdin rams (LowRFI: n = 1; HighRFI: n = 1) at the Virginia Tech Southwest Virginia Agricultural Research and Extension Center (SWAREC) to divergently select for RFI in their offspring (LowRFI vs. HighRFI). During lactation, ewes were fed a complete pellet (14% CP, 70% TDN) ad libitum (Mature ewes: 54 days; Yearling ewes: 53 days) and RFI calculated as the difference between actual and expected DMI (DMI predicted from ADG and metabolic body size). Feeding duration per meal, DMI per meal, and feeder visit frequency were analyzed to determine feeding behavior. Ewes were categorized as either LowRFI (RFI < 0) or HighRFI (RFI > 0) based on their RFI as a growing lamb. Statistical analyses were performed using PROC Mixed SAS (SAS Institute, Cary, NC). RFI category assigned from her performance as a lamb did not impact mature lactating ewe predictions for daily DMI, G:F, RFI, meal duration, DMI per meal or visit frequency (P > 0.10). However, RFI category had a significant effect on yearling lactating ewe daily DMI and RFI (P < 0.05). HighRFI yearling lactating ewes had greater daily DMI compared to LowRFI ewes (4.81 vs. 3.80 kg/day; P < 0.05). HighRFI yearling lactating ewes exhibited elevated RFI values compared to LowRFI ewes (0.09 vs. -0.05 kg; P < 0.05). RFI category did not impact yearling lactating ewe predictions for G:F, meal duration, DMI per meal or visit frequency (P > 0.10). Only 54% of mature lactating ewes remained in their predicted RFI category based on their RFI as a lamb while 82% of yearling lactating ewes remained in their predicted RFI category (P > 0.10). Inconsistencies in RFI prediction between mature and yearling ewe groups indicates the potential for genetic selection to impact lifetime feed efficiency with increased selection pressure. Further studies are required to evaluate lifetime maternal RFI trends.
